description: Global Shipping Traffic Density is a set of six raster layers counting the AIS positions reported by ships in each grid cell: commercial ships, fishing ships, oil and gas (platforms, rigs and FPSOs only), passenger ships, leisure vessels, and all ship categories combined. The rasters were created from the IMF's analysis of hourly AIS positions received between January 2015 and February 2021, obtained through a partnership with the IMF World Seaborne Trade Monitoring System (Cerdeiro, Komaromi, Liu and Saeed, 2020), with analysis supported by the World Bank ESMAP and PROBLUE programmes for its Offshore Wind Development Program. Coverage is the global ocean at 0.005 degree cells, about 500 m at the Equator. The layers are zipped downloads of 20 MB to 510 MB from the World Bank Data Catalog (version 5, files dated May 2021), classified Public and licensed CC BY 4.0, free. Caveats: positions come from moving and stationary ships alike, so the density shows general intensity of activity, not transits, and the layers are a single multi-year aggregate that is not updated. The data serve maritime network flow and hazard exposure analysis, siting and capacity planning for offshore wind and ports, and complement the IMF PortWatch port activity series catalogued here.
